draft.title: Measuring human resource effectiveness
card: A business can check how well it manages its people by looking at data. High staff turnover (the rate at which employees leave and are replaced) and high absenteeism (unplanned time away from work) can signal poor morale or poor conditions.
A high number of workplace accidents can point to unsafe conditions or weak training. A high level of disputes can point to problems with pay, conditions or management decisions.
Worker satisfaction surveys ask employees directly how they feel about their work. The results show problems that numbers alone may not reveal.
Benchmarking compares a business's results with those of other businesses, or with its own past results. It shows whether the business is doing better or worse than a standard.
draft.remember: Staff data, surveys and benchmarking show how well a business manages its people.

a.q: A retailer finds that many staff are leaving within six months and sick days are rising. What does this most likely suggest?
opts: Its human resource management may have weaknesses
Its human resource management is working well
Its staff are too well paid to stay motivated
Its products are poorly priced for customers
a.why: High turnover and rising absenteeism can signal poor morale or conditions, so the people management may have weaknesses. They do not suggest it is working well, which would show as low turnover and low absenteeism.
a.clue: Think about what staff leaving and missing work can signal.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Newcastle. She compares her staff turnover with the average for other bakeries in her region. Which method is she using?
opts: Benchmarking
A worker satisfaction survey
Measuring absenteeism
Counting workplace accidents
b.why: Benchmarking compares a business's results with those of other businesses or a standard. Priya is using turnover data, but the method is the comparison. A survey would ask her employees directly, which she has not done.
b.clue: Look at what she compares her result against.

a.best: Its human resource management may have weaknesses

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may have weaknesses'). It also sits beside its direct opposite ('is working well'), so a student could pick it from the wording without knowing the idea.

a.q: A retailer finds that many staff are leaving within six months and sick days are rising. What might this suggest?
opts: Staff morale or working conditions may be poor
Staff may be too well paid to stay motivated
Customers may be unhappy with the store's prices
Staff may be more satisfied than at rival stores
a.why: High turnover and rising absenteeism can signal poor morale or poor conditions. Staff who were more satisfied than elsewhere would be more likely to stay and turn up, not leave. Customer views on prices are not measured by staff data.
a.clue: Think about what staff leaving and missing work can signal.
